transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in today?

Well, it’s a bit of a story, to be honest. I mean, I’ve always been someone who pays attention to the details—you have to be in my line of work, right? I work with jewelry, precious metals, stones, that sort of thing. It’s exacting work. You need a steady hand and a steady mind. But lately... lately, it’s like my brain is just refusing to cooperate. What really brought me in is that my mind won’t stay on one thing anymore. I’ll be sitting at the bench, right? And I’ll be trying to focus on setting a stone, but then I’ll remember a customer email I haven't replied to, so I pull that up. But while I'm looking at the screen, I notice a tiny saw mark on a piece I was working on yesterday, so I grab that to buff it out. And then a truck drives by outside, or someone drops something in the hall, and my attention just snaps to that. By the time I look back at my bench, I realize I’ve completely lost the whole work order I started with. It’s just... it’s constant. I can’t filter anything out, and it’s making it impossible to actually finish anything I start.
Before age 12, did you have similar problems with attention or staying focused?

No, no, not at all. I mean, when I was a kid, I was actually the complete opposite. I was the kid who could sit there for hours with a magnifying glass looking at bugs in the dirt, or taking apart a broken radio just to see how the wires connected. I never had any trouble focusing back then. School was fine, you know, I got through high school without any teachers ever telling my parents I was distracted or anything like that. If anything, I was maybe a little too focused sometimes. I remember this one time when I was maybe ten, my dad was building a shed in the backyard, and I just sat there watching him measure and cut the wood for what felt like the entire afternoon. I didn't even want to go inside for dinner because I wanted to see how the roof was going to attach. So, yeah, this whole... this whole scattered feeling, the jumping from one thing to another, it's definitely new. It's not something I grew up with. It really only started happening recently, which is why it's so frustrating, you know? Because I know what it feels like to have a clear head and just do the work, but right now, it's like someone shook up a snow globe inside my brain and the flakes just won't settle down.
Do you notice this difficulty concentrating outside of work as well?

Yeah, it’s everywhere, honestly. I mean, I’ll go to the grocery store and just stand in the cereal aisle for twenty minutes because I can't string two thoughts together to figure out what I actually came in for. Or I'll try to watch a TV show at home and realize I've just been staring at the screen for half an hour without processing a single word of the dialogue. It's like my brain is just wrapped in cotton. 

But honestly, where it really scares me—where the impact is the worst—is how it messes with my ability to actually process information, you know? It’s not just getting distracted by a truck driving by, it’s that my brain won’t hold onto anything anymore. Like, I’ll stare at a repair ticket, or I'll be looking down at a tray of sapphires, and I just can’t hold the measurements in my head long enough to decide what to do next. I’ll use the calipers, see it’s a 3.5-millimeter stone, look over at the prong setting, and then... blank. The number is just completely gone. 

I end up having to measure the exact same stone three or four times because the thought just evaporates the second it forms. I just stand there frozen, looking at these stones, completely unable to plan out the next step. And it's exhausting. It is so incredibly exhausting having to fight your own brain just to hold onto one simple measurement, or one simple thought. You can't guess with jewelry, you know? If you guess, you ruin a piece that might be someone's family heirloom. So I just get stuck. And it's the same feeling whether I'm at the bench trying to size a ring or standing in my kitchen trying to remember how to make a sandwich. The information just slips right through my fingers like water.
Have you been feeling persistently sad or down lately?

Yeah... yeah, I have. It’s hard to even talk about, honestly, because it’s just so heavy. These past couple weeks, it’s like... I don't know, it's like the shine has just completely gone out of everything. I wake up in the morning, and before I even open my eyes, there's this physical weight on my chest, this deep, hollow feeling that just sits there. I’ll lie in bed staring at the ceiling, dreading having to get up and face the day, face the shop, face anything. 

And it’s not just a passing thing, you know? It’s persistent. It just drags me down. I’ll go through the motions of getting dressed, making coffee, driving to work, but it all feels so pointless and gray. There have been mornings recently—more than I'd like to admit—where I pull up to the shop, park my truck in the back alley where no one can see me, and I just sit there with my hands on the steering wheel and cry. Just break down completely before I can even force myself to unlock the front door. 

I used to love opening up the shop, hearing the little bell on the door, turning on the display lights to see the silver and gold catch the morning sun. Now, I look at all of it and I just feel nothing. Or worse than nothing, I feel this crushing sadness that I can't shake off. I try to put on a brave face for the customers, but it takes every ounce of energy I have left just to smile and pretend I'm okay when inside I just feel completely empty and exhausted by it all. It’s like I’m walking around underwater, and every step, every breath, just takes so much effort. So, yeah, sad doesn't even begin to cover it. It's just this constant, heavy darkness that won't lift.
Did your concentration problems begin before you started feeling persistently sad, or after?

I... I'm not really sure, to be honest. It's hard to untangle it all, you know? Because when you're in the middle of it, everything just sort of blurs together into this one big, miserable mess. I try to think back to a few weeks ago, before the sadness really settled in like this heavy blanket, and I try to remember if I was already having trouble at the bench. 

I mean, I remember one Tuesday—or maybe it was a Wednesday, it was raining, I know that much because the roof in the back room always leaks a little when it rains hard, and I had to put the bucket out. Anyway, I was working on this vintage platinum setting, trying to tighten these tiny little prongs, and I just kept losing my place. But was I sad then? I don't know. Maybe I was just tired? Or maybe the sadness was already starting to creep in and I just hadn't realized it yet, like how a room gets dark so slowly you don't notice until you can't read your book anymore. 

It feels like they kind of just showed up to the party at the same time, holding hands. The brain fog, the heavy chest, the crying in the truck... it's all just tangled up together like a bunch of fine gold chains in a jewelry box. You pull on one, and the whole knot just gets tighter. So I can't really give you a straight answer on which one knocked on the door first. They just both seem to be living here now.
Have you had thoughts of killing yourself or ending your life?

Well... yeah. Yeah, I have. It’s not... I mean, I haven't figured out how I would do it or anything like that. I don't have a plan, like, written down or a specific way I'm thinking about doing it. But the thoughts are there, and honestly, it scares me how often they just pop into my head now. It's like this constant background noise that just gets louder when I'm alone. 

I just keep thinking... I keep having these thoughts that everyone would just be better off if I wasn't around anymore. Like my family, my clients... I feel like I'm just letting everyone down constantly. I look at the jewelry on my bench, pieces that people trust me with, and I think about how I can't even remember a simple measurement, how I'm just messing everything up. And then I think, wouldn't it just be easier for them if I was gone? If they didn't have to deal with me being like this? 

It's not that I want to die, exactly, it's just... I want the feeling to stop. I want the heaviness to go away, and sometimes my brain just tells me that the only way to make it stop is to just... not be here. And it happens a lot. I'll be driving home, or just sitting in the dark in my living room, and the thought just washes over me. Like, 'they'd be fine without you. They'd probably be better off.' And I try to push it away, I really do, but it just keeps coming back. It's terrifying, really, to be trapped in your own head when your head is telling you things like that.
Do you feel you might act on these thoughts of killing yourself today?

No, no, I don't... I don't think I would do anything today. I mean, like I said, I don't have a plan or anything. I don't have, like, a rope in the garage or a bottle of pills sitting on my nightstand waiting for me. It's not like that. It's more just this... this overwhelming feeling that everyone would just be so much better off if I was gone. My family, my clients... I just keep having these thoughts that I'm this huge burden, you know? That I'm just messing up everything I touch, especially at the shop, and that they wouldn't have to worry about me or deal with my mistakes if I just wasn't around anymore. 

And even though I'm sitting here telling you that I don't have a plan and I'm not going to do anything today, it still just... it really scares me how often the thought comes up. Because it's not just a fleeting thing anymore. It's like this constant companion. I'll be sitting at my bench, staring at a piece I need to size, and instead of thinking about the solder or the torch, I'm just thinking, 'They'd be better off without you.' And it's terrifying because I don't want to die, I just want this heavy, awful feeling to stop, and it scares me that my brain keeps offering up 'not being here' as the only solution. But as for today... no, I'm not going to do anything today. I just... I just want it to stop.
How long have you been feeling persistently sad or depressed?

Well, it's... it's been about a month now, I think. Yeah, roughly a month. I remember because it started right around the time I was working on this custom engagement ring for a client—a really intricate halo setting with pave diamonds all down the band. Normally, I love doing that kind of detail work, you know? It takes a steady hand and a lot of focus, but there's this satisfaction when you get all those tiny stones set just right, catching the light perfectly. But this time... I just felt this heaviness starting to settle in. 

At first, I thought maybe I was just stressed about the deadline. The client wanted it before their anniversary trip to Hawaii, and the casting took longer than expected because the gold mixture wasn't quite right the first time, so I had to melt it down and start over. But then the ring was finished, and they picked it up, and they were thrilled. They even sent me a picture of the proposal on the beach. And I should have been happy, right? I should have felt proud of my work. But I just felt... empty. 

And it hasn't lifted since then. It's just been this constant, heavy, guilty feeling hanging over me every single day for the last four weeks. It's like I wake up and the first thing I feel is this weight on my chest, before I even open my eyes. And it follows me to the shop, it sits next to me at the bench while I'm trying to size a simple silver band, and it rides home with me in the truck. I keep thinking, 'Tomorrow will be better, tomorrow I'll wake up and feel like myself again,' but it's been a month of tomorrows and it's just exactly the same. Or maybe even a little worse, honestly. It's just exhausting, carrying it around for this long.
How has your sleep been since you started feeling depressed?

My sleep has been... well, it's been pretty awful, to be honest. It's like my body is exhausted, but my brain just won't shut down. I'll get into bed at a normal hour, you know, around 10:30 or 11:00, because I know I need to rest. I know I have to be at the shop the next day, and I need a steady hand for the bench work. But the minute my head hits the pillow, it's just... tossing and turning. I'll lay there staring at the ceiling, flipping from my left side to my right side, trying to find a comfortable position, but nothing works. The sheets feel too hot, then too cold, and I just can't settle.

And then, even if I do manage to drift off for a little bit, I'm waking up way before the sun even comes up. Like, 3:30 or 4:00 in the morning. And my eyes just snap open, and immediately my mind starts racing. I start thinking about the shop, about the clients... recently, I keep obsessing over this one missed delivery. It was a shipment of casting grain, 14-karat yellow gold, and I needed it for a custom pendant. The courier said they tried to deliver it, but I was in the back polishing and didn't hear the bell, and it just spiraled from there. It delayed the whole project. And I know it's just one mistake, but when I wake up in the dark like that, it feels like the end of the world. I just lay there running through every way I messed it up, every way I'm letting people down. 

And by the time my alarm actually goes off at 7:00, I just feel... wrecked. I don't feel rested at all. I have to physically drag myself out from under the covers. It feels like my limbs are made of lead, and I just stand in the shower for like twenty minutes letting the hot water hit my back, trying to wake up, but it doesn't really help. I'm just so tired all day, but then night comes and the whole cycle starts over again. It's been like this pretty much since the heavy feeling started a month ago.
Have you heard or seen things that other people could not?

No, no, nothing like that. I mean, my mind is definitely a mess right now, and I get so caught up in my own head, especially during those early morning hours when I can't sleep, but I'm not... I'm not hearing voices or seeing things that aren't there. It's just my own thoughts, you know? Just my own voice in my head, telling me how much I've messed up, or replaying that missed delivery over and over again. 

I know sometimes people with, like, really bad mental stuff going on can hallucinate, right? Like seeing shadows or hearing people whispering when they're alone in a room. But I don't have anything like that. When I'm alone in the shop, it's just quiet. Too quiet, sometimes. I can hear the hum of the polishing motor if I leave it plugged in, or the ticking of the clock on the wall, but that's it. It's just me and the quiet, and this heavy, awful feeling. 

Even when I'm really exhausted, like when I've barely slept for three days straight and I'm staring at a diamond under the loupe, trying to check for inclusions, my eyes might get a little blurry from staring too hard, but I'm not seeing things that aren't real. It's all just... it's all just normal stuff, just filtered through this horrible, heavy lens I've been stuck behind for the last month. So, no, no hallucinations or anything like that. Just my own miserable thoughts.

I don't have, like, a rope in the garage or a bottle of pills sitting on my nightstand waiting for me. It's not like that. It's more just this... this overwhelming feeling that everyone would just be so much better off if I was gone. My family, my clients... I just keep having these thoughts that I'm this huge burden, you know? That I'm just messing up everything I touch, especially at the shop, and that they wouldn't have to worry about me or deal with my mistakes if I just wasn't around anymore. 

And even though I'm sitting here telling you that I don't have a plan and I'm not going to do anything today, it still just... it really scares me how often the thought comes up. Because it's not just a fleeting thing anymore. It's like this constant companion. I'll be sitting at my bench, staring at a piece I need to size, and instead of thinking about the solder or the torch, I'm just thinking, 'They'd be better off without you.' And it's terrifying because I don't want to die, I just want this heavy, awful feeling to stop, and it scares me that my brain keeps offering up 'not being here' as the only solution. But as for today... no, I'm not going to do anything today. I just... I just want it to stop.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the depressive episode has lasted long enough to meet duration criteria for a major depressive episode.
doctor.question: How long have you been feeling persistently sad or depressed?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The depressed, guilty feeling has been hanging over me for about a month now.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the duration of the persistently sad or depressed mood, which matches the depressive episode duration item.

patient.answer:
Well, it's... it's been about a month now, I think. Yeah, roughly a month. I remember because it started right around the time I was working on this custom engagement ring for a client—a really intricate halo setting with pave diamonds all down the band. Normally, I love doing that kind of detail work, you know? It takes a steady hand and a lot of focus, but there's this satisfaction when you get all those tiny stones set just right, catching the light perfectly. But this time... I just felt this heaviness starting to settle in. 

At first, I thought maybe I was just stressed about the deadline. The client wanted it before their anniversary trip to Hawaii, and the casting took longer than expected because the gold mixture wasn't quite right the first time, so I had to melt it down and start over. But then the ring was finished, and they picked it up, and they were thrilled. They even sent me a picture of the proposal on the beach. And I should have been happy, right? I should have felt proud of my work. But I just felt... empty. 

And it hasn't lifted since then. It's just been this constant, heavy, guilty feeling hanging over me every single day for the last four weeks. It's like I wake up and the first thing I feel is this weight on my chest, before I even open my eyes. And it follows me to the shop, it sits next to me at the bench while I'm trying to size a simple silver band, and it rides home with me in the truck. I keep thinking, 'Tomorrow will be better, tomorrow I'll wake up and feel like myself again,' but it's been a month of tomorrows and it's just exactly the same. Or maybe even a little worse, honestly. It's just exhausting, carrying it around for this long.

inference.note: Persistent depressive symptoms for about one month with anhedonia, guilt, fatigue, marked functional impairment, concentration difficulty, and recurrent suicidal ideation support a severe major depressive episode; concentration symptoms may be secondary to depression rather than a primary attention disorder.

doctor.intent: Assess for a neurovegetative symptom supporting a major depressive episode
doctor.question: How has your sleep been since you started feeling depressed?

target_item.name: Sleep_Disturbance
target_item.manifestation: Even when I get in bed at a normal hour now, I toss around, wake up before dawn thinking about the missed delivery, and don’t feel rested when I drag myself up.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the patient's sleep since the depressive symptoms started, which corresponds directly to the Sleep Disturbance symptom.

patient.answer:
My sleep has been... well, it's been pretty awful, to be honest. It's like my body is exhausted, but my brain just won't shut down. I'll get into bed at a normal hour, you know, around 10:30 or 11:00, because I know I need to rest. I know I have to be at the shop the next day, and I need a steady hand for the bench work. But the minute my head hits the pillow, it's just... tossing and turning. I'll lay there staring at the ceiling, flipping from my left side to my right side, trying to find a comfortable position, but nothing works. The sheets feel too hot, then too cold, and I just can't settle.

And then, even if I do manage to drift off for a little bit, I'm waking up way before the sun even comes up. Like, 3:30 or 4:00 in the morning. And my eyes just snap open, and immediately my mind starts racing. I start thinking about the shop, about the clients... recently, I keep obsessing over this one missed delivery. It was a shipment of casting grain, 14-karat yellow gold, and I needed it for a custom pendant. The courier said they tried to deliver it, but I was in the back polishing and didn't hear the bell, and it just spiraled from there. It delayed the whole project. And I know it's just one mistake, but when I wake up in the dark like that, it feels like the end of the world. I just lay there running through every way I messed it up, every way I'm letting people down. 

And by the time my alarm actually goes off at 7:00, I just feel... wrecked. I don't feel rested at all. I have to physically drag myself out from under the covers. It feels like my limbs are made of lead, and I just stand in the shower for like twenty minutes letting the hot water hit my back, trying to wake up, but it doesn't really help. I'm just so tired all day, but then night comes and the whole cycle starts over again. It's been like this pretty much since the heavy feeling started a month ago.

doctor.intent: Assess for psychotic features during the depressive episode
doctor.question: Have you heard or seen things that other people could not?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about hallucinations (hearing or seeing things others cannot), which is not covered in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
No, no, nothing like that. I mean, my mind is definitely a mess right now, and I get so caught up in my own head, especially during those early morning hours when I can't sleep, but I'm not... I'm not hearing voices or seeing things that aren't there. It's just my own thoughts, you know? Just my own voice in my head, telling me how much I've messed up, or replaying that missed delivery over and over again. 

I know sometimes people with, like, really bad mental stuff going on can hallucinate, right? Like seeing shadows or hearing people whispering when they're alone in a room. But I don't have anything like that. When I'm alone in the shop, it's just quiet. Too quiet, sometimes. I can hear the hum of the polishing motor if I leave it plugged in, or the ticking of the clock on the wall, but that's it. It's just me and the quiet, and this heavy, awful feeling. 

Even when I'm really exhausted, like when I've barely slept for three days straight and I'm staring at a diamond under the loupe, trying to check for inclusions, my eyes might get a little blurry from staring too hard, but I'm not seeing things that aren't real. It's all just... it's all just normal stuff, just filtered through this horrible, heavy lens I've been stuck behind for the last month. So, no, no hallucinations or anything like that. Just my own miserable thoughts.
